text: If you're looking for something simple, I'd recommend other clinics. The queue here is quite long. If you come at 6 PM in the evening, the female doctor is already rushing home. It might be more suitable for patients with underlying medical conditions who are already receiving treatment at the hospital, as the information is linked. However, I think other clinics manage their schedules better. If you arrive on time or even half an hour early, you won't have to wait, which can cause your appointment to be pushed back, affecting the next person in line. I recommend allowing extra time for your dental treatment. If you know what your next appointment will involve, allow extra time for other patients. This way, you won't have to wait much longer than your scheduled appointment time almost every time. It might be better to learn about the system from related dental clinics. Since you can't just walk in, you have to book an appointment in advance anyway.

Previously, the doctor recommended an X-ray for my child, which revealed two impacted wisdom teeth on each side. During school break, my child called to inquire about the cost of the surgery. After asking several times, they were told that the procedure is charged per side (left and right), and the doctor would perform it one side at a time, both upper and lower, at 4,000-6,000 baht per side depending on the complexity (not charged per tooth like in Bangkok). My child wanted to save money and suggested we travel from Bangkok to have it done here. After the procedure, they informed us that the service fee was charged per side. When we inquired about accountability, we were met with silence. In addition to the cost of travel, accommodation, contacting the doctor, and paying for suture removal ourselves in Bangkok, it was our own fault. We didn't fully believe the initial explanation about charging per side, and we wanted to try it out. My child wanted to save money, so we should have supported them. However, my child has learned and become more cautious about how these semi-governmental organizations operate and their level of responsibility towards patients. The receipts we received were from both the doctor and the hospital, with the split roughly 50:50.
